about: The bar for video production quality, held in the three layers Krish asked for on 29 October 2026. The floor is the eight nevers Krish confirmed on 29 October 2026 (ruling 12), each citing his earlier words or the rule it rests on, and the gate that already holds it, or held at review where none does yet: the only refusals this bar adds, while existing gates and the rejection floor's approved standards refuse as they do. The aims are what great looks like: the cuts he named, the brand book and his own words, with the fifteen qualities and the reference moments as things to aim at and compare against, never a checklist. Under test are choices he made for now, each the current default, recorded per piece on the making record and judged on real engagement. The page is docs/production/THE_BAR.md; this file names the reference files exactly, says how each one's identity was confirmed, lists the reference moments and each quality's comparison points by timestamp, and carries his words and rulings. The page and this file must agree (python3 scripts/floor.py --check). scripts/floor.py prints the bar for the makers in full_bar_for_makers and a one-line pointer for the other makers in applies_to_makers, before the rejection standards. Only Krish adds a reference, changes the bar or moves its standing from draft to approved.

taste.about: how he wants taste held: the bar reads in three layers, the floor, the aims and what is under test; his words open the page and lead the printout
taste.words: I hope you understand that I would much rather the engine know what kind of thing doesn't fly with me, rather than implement incredibly specific rules everywhere which came from feedback on one piece of content for one specific reason. We're still in the test-and-learn phase of what works and what doesn't, and finding our feet on all of this stuff but there are some clear floor nervos and some clear aspirationals to aim at

ruling.words: the video production quality standards for the latest Friday (AI Passports) and Monday (character.ai) pieces are the floor for what I expect in terms of premium quality, motion design, cinematic feeling, movement, branding etc. Friday's is a voiceover format and Monday's a regular split screen format. Do not be intensely literal here as every piece is different, but I want you to get a feel for the standards we are never to fall beneath ever again
ruling.quote: Do not be intensely literal here as every piece is different, but I want you to get a feel for the standards we are never to fall beneath ever again
ruling.correction: the long voiceover video is still being post produced so dont just assume that the voiceover format only has a 90sec version, you are only to look for production quality standards

general.about: how every video should be made; his words lead the aims
general.words:
In general I think:
- minimal random components and labels
- good motion design
- good animation
- good visuals

Keep it simple but keep it classy and on brand. I'd stick to the brand book for now.

standing_note: The floor is his, confirmed on 29 October (ruling 12). The aims are the engine's reading of the cuts he named; he has not approved their wording except where it quotes him. Aim at them; only he approves them.
principle: Every frame designed and owned by the brand; pictures and motion that add meaning beyond the words; light, depth and material; the brand as a system; real, dated proof; finished sound. Put each new moment beside a reference moment, in motion, at full size, with sound: would it sit beside it without looking cheaper, flatter, slower, busier or less owned? Never copy the references; each piece finds its own objects, devices and big moments.
measured_values: Context about the references, never targets. Lengths, shapes, cut counts, frame timings, levels, tempo and sampled colours describe these three files only. They are kept out of config/reference-cuts.json on purpose, and floor.py --check refuses a measured field written there (duration, aspect, bpm, lufs and the like); it cannot see a figure inside a sentence, so none is written in one either. The existing gates set the only numeric limits.

floor.about: The only refusals this bar adds on taste, while existing gates and the rejection floor's approved standards refuse as they do: the eight nevers Krish confirmed on 29 October 2026 (ruling 12), in his order. Each keeps the list's words he confirmed (listed), the question's own wording (asked), his earlier words or the rule it rests on, and the gate that already holds it, or held at review where none does yet. No other refusal, gate, lint pattern or required field is added from feedback on one piece; everything else is an aim, a choice under test or an example of the kind of thing that does not fly.

under_test.about: Choices Krish made for now, to be judged on real engagement (his words: "we need to test and learn"). Each is the current default, never a refusal and never written as a never. Each piece records which it used on its making record, so a retrospective can join the choice to how the piece did. To change a default, change it here: the creative direction's template and the record read it from this file.

choices.title: The hook is the intro
choices.what: Friday 23's way: the first frame is the hook in the brand's dress, logo and series tag in the corners from the start; no story card or logo intro; one calm close, held long enough to read.

choices.title: The lead picture, chosen per piece
choices.what: The storyboard he signs shows both as stills, the series picture from the brand book and a story object, Claude's pick marked; his signature accepts it unless he ticks the other.

choices.title: One sound on the big moment
choices.what: One sound under a piece's biggest moment, such as a low thud as BANKRUPT slams in, and nothing anywhere else. None until he approves a small set by ear (approved_set); Epidemic Sound covers sound effects (his yes, 29 Oct), and no spend is assumed.

qualities.name: Premium finish: every frame looks made and owned
Pictures that explain: every part adds meaning
Motion craft: weight, ease, stagger, exits
Cinematic feel: light, focus, depth, a living world
Movement and pace: alive, and timed to meaning
Typography: few voices, fixed jobs, words that add
Composition and layout: the whole frame, one focal point
Colour and grade: an owned palette where colour means something
Texture and depth: material, never a flat template
Captions: burned in, branded, calm, in sync
Proof visuals: real, dated and designed
Krish on camera: real, steady, in sync

reference_moments.what: USING A / CHINESE AI? builds on a living phone plate, with headline, coral slab, italic deck, word-by-word caption and a card tracked into the screen. The opening statement and the type system.
The CHESKY TO BLOOMBERG quote card tracked into the phone while the plate sways, with a hand-drawn underline and server racks soft behind. Cinematic plate and named source.
A dark brand beat; TWO PASSPORTS lands first, then the page rises and fades up. A chapter transition.
The CHINA stamp slams in oversized and tilted, then settles. Motion with weight.
A mint marker loop drawn round CHINA in a few frames. Hand-drawn emphasis on the one thing that matters.
Passport paper with grain, security lines, halftone round the flag and stickers with offset shadows. Texture.
'? OUT OF 3' held back, then filled to 2. A number withheld until it is proved.
Headline, a phone card with a circled entry, a caption and a mint band, all four readable. Composition.
The phone swings and pushes into the dated DeepSeek screen recording, with the sentence underlined and quoted. The signature move, spent on the proof.
The OUR CALL card held to be read while the captions step aside. A read-hold and caption discipline.
The caption slab becomes the brand band strapped across the passport. A branded close that completes the metaphor.
The story card builds piece by piece in reading order. Staggered build, the craft only: the hook is now the intro (under test).
MILLIONS MADE FRIENDS HERE arrives word by word as spoken while the grid spreads. Type in time with speech.
The BANKRUPT impact (flash, oversized slam, crawling tapes, debris) while the grid loses its colour. A big moment, with colour telling the story.
A torn-edged receipt rises, its lines build, and its mint figure matches the caption's mint chip. Texture, proof and captions speaking one language.
An article blurred except for the quoted phrase. Focus used as a lens, and honest proof.
THE PEOPLE rides an arrow into Disney's slot while THE LAWSUITS stays behind. Motion that explains.
Empty slots fill as each company is named, then the counter slows hard into 75%. State change on the word.
One end card, its lines revealed one at a time, the underline drawing on. One close.
Measured, not yet heard: the music under the opening story card, a low bed under the hook and a tight voice edit. Sound finish.
A stage with a grid, two drifting light pools and a vignette. A lit ground.
Logos drop into the RENTED box. A transition that carries the thought on.
A slow push on the CTO document with one phrase in focus, then it defocuses as the receipt springs up and settles. Cinematic hold, transition and craft.
Comparison receipts count up into a side-by-side board. Proof that sums up.
The counter rolls to 75% on 'I'm 75% sure'. A state change on the word.
